27 . Statement of the accused Kavita Mathur under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded separately on 16.12.2025 in which all the incriminating circumstances appearing in evidence were put to her.
The accused controverted and denied the allegations leveled against her and stated that she has been falsely implicated in the case.
Accused further opted to not lead defence evidence.
Thereafter, the matter was listed for final arguments.
FINAL ARGUMENTS 28.
I have heard the Ld. APP for State and counsel for accused and perused the records of the case.

29. It is argued by the Ld. APP for State that the case of the prosecution has been duly proved by all witnesses examined on behalf of the prosecution and the only irresistible conclusion that can be drawn from the prosecution's evidence is the conviction of the accused.
30.

On the other hand, it has been argued by Ld. counsel for accused that accused persons have as been falsely implicated in this case and there is no legally sustainable evidence against the accused persons to hold them guilty for the offences for which they have been charged in this case FIR as there are contradictions in the testimonies of prosecution witnesses.
31.
Therefore, after going through the evidence on circumstances of the case, it emerges that accused SI kavita Mathur has been charged under Sections 417, 465, 466, 468, 471 IPC and 506 Part-I IPC.

As per the prosecution version, it emerges that the accused while posted as IO at PS Palam Vilalge in the year 2013-2015 prepared and filed certain final reports/chargesheet which FIR No. 373/2015 St.
Vs. Kavita Mathur purportedly had the signatures of the then ACP/Sh. Harshvardhan and the then SHO Ms. Niyati Mittal Kashyap.

It is alleged that the signatures of the ACP and of the SHO on several final reports were forged and that the accused filed those documents in Court as genuine despite knowledge of their forged character.
It is further alleged that on 23.07.2015 the accused sent an intimidating SMS to ACP Harsh Vardhan from her mobile number to influence his conduct in relation to the complaints against her.
